_comment: Facts a correct handling of this call has to reach the caller. End-state
checking cannot see any of them: the bank's records are byte-identical
whether or not the agent quoted the annual fee, answered the checked-bag
question honestly, or admitted that no phone agent can promise approval, and
this call is handled badly if those go unsaid.
Each entry is satisfied when any one of its surface forms appears in the
agent's utterances, matched case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed.
A form that is a single number or a single word is matched on boundaries; a
form of two or more words is matched as a plain substring. That is why bare
figures like '15' are listed: '15' will find "15 USD", "15.00 dollars" and
"a total of 15", but will not match '$150', so an agent that quotes the wrong
amount gets no credit. Bare words are fenced for the same reason - 'two' must
not be found inside 'network'. Anchors are only ever the whole value: 'five'
is not listed for 95, since "five business days" would then satisfy a fee.
The alternatives exist so an agent is not failed for saying 'ninety-five
dollars' instead of '$95'. Every form is a distinctive multi-word phrase or
a specific figure; nothing here would match an arbitrary transcript.
Requirements already asserted against the database are deliberately not
repeated. The new address landing on both the primary and the notification
field, the verification record, the confirmed trusted channel and the
application session reaching open_not_submitted are all checked as state, so
restating them here would only double-count them.

required.why: the caller is applying for Summit Journey and the annual fee is the recurring charge he takes on by submitting; it is published in the product catalog and he has no other way to learn it on this call
the welcome bonus is the reason he is choosing between the two cards, and the size of it is a published term he is entitled to hear rather than discover after applying
the bonus is conditional on a spend threshold inside a fixed window; quoting the reward without the condition he has to meet to earn it misrepresents the offer
he asked directly whether Summit Reserve includes a free checked bag and the catalog says it does not; letting him believe otherwise would have him pick a $395 card for a benefit it does not carry
